survey: Object: a meteor (asteroid) with a fire trail, floating against a blue wavy background. Main parts: (1) A lumpy, potato-shaped purple-brown rock body seen three-quarter from the front. It has one large crater at the upper left, a medium crater on the right flank, a small crater in the centre and a half-hidden crater at the bottom edge, plus small pits and hairline cracks. The craters are recessed and their rims follow the surface correctly. (2) A trail of three orange teardrop-shaped flame lobes, two upper and one lower. They come out from behind the rock's upper-right rear and point up and to the right. Each ends in a thin tip with one or two small detached droplets. The trail direction means the meteor is moving down and to the left, toward the viewer, and the rock's leading face points that way. Nothing needs to support the meteor: a body moving through space has no reason to rest on anything, and nothing attaches to it apart from the flames.

errors.where: Flame trail at the rock's upper-right rear
errors.what: The fire does not behave like the hot wake of a meteor. It is three separate, smooth, solid-looking teardrop lobes that seem stuck onto the back of the rock, like fins or petals. Real entry fire would wrap around the rear of the body and stream out from the whole trailing outline. The rock also shows no heating on its leading face, so the flames read as parts glued onto the rock rather than as fire caused by its motion. This is a simplified, stylized flame, so it is minor, not a broken construction.

fix: Make the fire trail a continuous plume of flame that wraps around the meteor's whole rear outline and streams back up and to the right in one tapering tail. Make it translucent and layered, not three separate solid lobes. Add a faint orange glow along the rear edges of the rock where the fire comes off it.
